anne: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak landed on staging we see a CPU-side perf regression for short-chat workloads. P99 latency up ~30ms and host CPU up ~18% on the serving pods. :eyes:

raj: Any traces/commands we can use?

anne: I collected a quick perf + flamegraph on a staging replica (20s steady load). Command I used:
```bash
sudo perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -p $(pidof redwood_server) -- sleep 20
sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
Attached the SVG to the artifact bucket (/artifacts/flame/1912345678-flame.svg).

perf-bot: nsys trace created: s3://artifacts/nsys/1912345678.nsys

sasha: quick glance at flame.svg — the largest stacks are `schedule_batch` -> `handle_request` and a secondary hotspot in `tokenize_single`/`hash_table_lookup`. Looks like CPU is dominated by scheduler + tokenizer churn.

dominik: Could be GIL contention from Python-level batching code. Did the kernel selection change swap in a kernel variant that is more CPU-heavy per-token?

anne: Yes, kernel-selector picked `kernel_v3_quant_fast` instead of `kernel_v2`. A/B test: forcing v2 brings CPU down to baseline. Numbers from perf report (sampled):
```
Samples: 10000, Event: cycles
  52.4%  redwood_server  [.] schedule_batch
  24.8%  redwood_server  [.] tokenize_single
  8.9%   libc-2.31.so    [.] futex_wait
  5.1%   libpthread.so   [.] pthread_mutex_lock
  4.2%   python3         [.] PyEval_EvalFrameEx
```

raj: Nice, that suggests kernel_v3 increases per-token CPU. Can you share the perf folded lines around schedule_batch -> tokenize?

anne: Pasted a small sample from out.folded for the hot path:
```
redwood_server;redwood_server;schedule_batch;handle_request;tokenize_single  320
redwood_server;redwood_server;schedule_batch;handle_request;kv_cache_lookup  180
redwood_server;tokenize_single;hash_table_lookup  150
```

infra-ci: FYI the new kernel regresses packing efficiency on small input sizes; microbenchmarks showed higher cycles/char for <512 tokens.

sasha: Short-term mitigation options:
- fallback routing: route requests <512 tokens to kernel_v2
- tweak batching heuristics: lower max batch size for short requests or increase coalescing timeout slightly so python scheduler spends less time thrashing
- disable prefix/KV cache for tiny requests (caches are causing extra hash lookups on hot path)

dominik: Also try a narrow perf sampling with `perf record -e cycles:u -F 200 -g -- sleep 30` to get user-only stacks; if we see lots of pthread/futex we know scheduler syncs are the problem.

anne: I ran user-only sampling as you suggested. Results: pthread/futex still present (contended locks around batch queue). Short test disabling KV cache reduced tokenize hotspot by ~11% but increased average latency for repeated prompts. Tradeoff.

raj: Actionable next steps?

anne: Proposed action items:
1) Run full nsys trace for a production-like distributed load to confirm kernel_v3 behavior on GPU side (nsys already generated).
2) Revert kernel-selector rollout to v2 for the short-request pool and monitor.
3) Experiment with batching heuristics: cap batch_size for short requests and bump coalescing timeout to reduce GIL thrash.
4) Long term: profile kernel_v3 to see which conv/attention kernels cost more CPU cycles per token and open tuning PRs to reduce that path.

dominik: SGTM. I'll take item 3 and run microbenchmarks for batching windows.

raj: I'll coordinate the rollback for the short-request pool this afternoon. Ping me when infra plan is ready.

perf-bot: Created perf-ticket #412: "kernel_v3 CPU regression (short-request pool)" (assignee: infra-team).

anne: Thanks all — I'll paste follow-up issue + perf artifacts in the ticket and mark the rollout paused for the short pool. :thumbsup:
